cases.name: Sarah Anne Zoelle
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Sarah attended Sioux City Schools, from Lincoln Elementary through West High School, attaining her GED through WITCC.  She worked at Coffee Works and Charlie’s Wine & Spirits for several years, greeting everyone with her contagious smile and with courtesy, kindness, and graciousness.  Recently she has been a stay-at-home-mom to her daughter Xyla Soul.  The loss of Sarah in our lives is beyond comprehension or adequate description.  To put into words her lasting effect on everyone she came into contact with defies words.  Sarah was a beautiful soul who touched people in a meaningful, non-judgmental, supportive, and unconditional way.  She is the oldest of eleven children who cared deeply, loved unconditionally, and met each one of her siblings at an individual and personal level.  Sarah’s loving impact will be carried by all those so graciously touched."

cases.name: Amanda Marissa "Mandy" De La O McCauley
cases.about:
Her obituary said: "She attended West High School in Sioux City, continued her education at Western Iowa Tech Community College, and graduated in 2011. Pursuing her love of dentistry, she became a valued member of the team at Lilly Family Dentistry, where she worked for many years. She formed many meaningful connections with both her coworkers and the families she served.

Amanda’s greatest joy and most cherished role was that of a mother. She welcomed her son in 2013 and her daughter in 2018. Her children were the most important part of her life, and she devoted herself wholeheartedly to them.

She loved life deeply. She loved her family, friends, work, music, dancing, and singing. She enjoyed watching movies and was fond of quoting her favorites, bringing humor and laughter into everyday moments. She was a fiercely loyal and caring daughter, sister, aunt, cousin, and friend.

Amanda’s warmth, laughter, kindness, and playful spirit touched countless lives. She will be deeply missed and forever loved. Her memory, strength, and loyalty will live on in the hearts of those who knew her, especially in the lives of her children."
cases.narrative: He shot and killed Mandy and her mother, then committed suicide.

cases.name: Yolanda Guerra Koon
cases.about: Her obituary said: "Yolanda was a pillar of the Siouxland community, helping new residents transition to their new surroundings and providing interpretation services at job sites and clinics. In addition, she offered comfort and support to victims of sexual assault and domestic violence. She was known for her heart of gold, unforgettable sense of humor, and vibrant personality. Yolanda was devoted to her Catholic faith. Her children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren were her greatest loves. She worked tirelessly to provide for, protect, and encourage them to enjoy life. She loved her family and friends deeply, often reaching out to make sure they knew she cared for them and remembered them."
